chunks: And as for what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to him (peace be upon him): A man married a woman and consummated the marriage with her, then she died. Is it permissible for him to marry her mother? He said: Glory be to Allah, how can her mother be permissible for him when he has consummated the marriage with her?

I said to him: And if she died before he consummated the marriage with her, is her mother permissible for him? He said: And what is the thing that becomes forbidden to him from her when he has not consummated the marriage with her?
Thus, the ruling in this narration is also what we said in the first two narrations.

It is all the same, given that Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, the narrator of this hadith, said 'I asked him' and did not specify who he was. It is possible that the one who asked him was not the Imam, from whose opinion one must return. Therefore, if this possibility holds, the objection based on it is nullified.
ai.seo_question: Is the mother of a deceased wife forbidden to her ex-husband if she died before consummation?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfabar clarifies the distinction between mere contract (nikah) and consummation (dakhala) in determining the prohibition of a wife's mother, affirming that consummation is the decisive factor for permanent prohibition. The text also includes a scholarly nuance regarding the identity of the questioner ('al-ladhi'), noting that if the questioner was not the specific Imam referenced in other reports, the potential contradiction is resolved, thereby reinforcing the reliability of the ruling.
